questions.question: The radius of a right circular cylinder is four times of its height. If the height of the cylinder is 14 cm, then what is the volume of cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of the cylinder = π × r² × h = (22 / 7) × 56 × 56 × 14

This simplifies to: 22 × 56 × 56 × 2

We can instantly find the answer by checking the unit digit of this product.

Unit digit product = 2 × 6 × 6 × 2 = 144, which ends in 4.

Looking at the given options, only 137984 has a unit digit of 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 137984 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the cylinder (h) = 14 cm

Radius of the cylinder (r) = 4 × height = 4 × 14 = 56 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a right circular cylinder = π × r² × h

 h = 14 cm
 Right Circular Cylinder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (22 / 7) × (56)² × 14

⇒ Volume = (22 / 7) × 56 × 56 × 14

⇒ Volume = 22 × 56 × 56 × 2

⇒ Volume = 44 × 3136

⇒ Volume = 137984 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 137984 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a Cylinder

The curved surface area includes only the outer side surface of the cylinder, excluding the top and bottom circular bases. Formula: CSA = 2 × π × r × h

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface area plus the area of both the top and bottom solid bases. Formula: TSA = 2 × π × r × (r + h)

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a corresponding cylinder will always have exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Formula: Volume = (1 / 3) × π × r² × h
</p

questions.question: Some medicine in liquid form is prepared in a hemispherical container of diameter 36 cm. When the container is full of medicine, the medicine is transferred to small cylindrical bottles of diameter 6 cm and height 6 cm. How many bottles are required to empty the container?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of hemispherical container = 36 cm ⇒ Radius (R) = 36 cm / 2 = 18 cm

Diameter of cylindrical bottles = 6 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 6 cm / 2 = 3 cm

Height of cylindrical bottles (h) = 6 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × π × R³

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ V_hemisphere = (2/3) × π × (18)³ 

⇒ V_cylinder = π × (3)² × 6

⇒ V_hemisphere = (2/3) × π × 5832 = 3888π cm³

⇒ V_cylinder = π × 9 × 6 = 54π cm³

Number
 of bottles required = V_hemisphere / V_cylinder

⇒ = 3888π / 54π = 72

**Hence, 72 bottles are required to empty the container.**

questions.question: What is the height (in m) of a conical water tank having radius of 70 m and volume of 46,200 m³? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for height of a cone: h = (3 × Volume) ÷ (π × r²)

⇒ h = (3 × 46200) ÷ (22/7 × 70 × 70)

⇒ h = 138600 ÷ 15400

⇒ h = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the conical tank (r) = 70 m

Volume of the conical tank (V) = 46,200 m³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0323609435983406ed6456f87034b5d28e33900b105be1af6915d29386f6a1b3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 46200 = 1/3 × 22/7 × 70 × 70 × h

⇒ 46200 = 1/3 × 22 × 10 × 70 × h

⇒ 46200 = 15400/3 × h

⇒ h = (46200 × 3) ÷ 15400

⇒ h = 3 × 3 = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of a Cone

It is the distance from the apex to any point on the circumference of the base: l = √(r² + h²)

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface (excluding the base) is given by: CSA = π × r × l

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = π × r × (r + l)
</p

questions.question: The difference between the total surface area and lateral surface area of a cube, if side of the cube is 11 cm (in square cm), is _________ .

Difference between TSA and LSA = TSA - LSA

**Calculation:**

Side = 11 cm

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 6 × (11)²

TSA = 6 × 121

TSA = 726 cm²

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 4 × (11)²

LSA = 484 cm²

Difference between TSA and LSA = TSA - LSA

⇒ 726 - 484

⇒ 242 cm²

**The difference between the total surface area and lateral surface area of the cube is 242 cm².**

questions.question: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 5%, then by what percentage will the surface area of the sphere increase?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius of a sphere is increased by 5%. 

**Formula used:**

Surface Area of Sphere = 4πr²

**Calculation:**

Let the original radius be r.

New radius = r + 5% of r = r + 0.05r = 1.05r

Original surface area = 4πr²

New surface area = 4π(1.05r)²

⇒ New surface area = 4π(1.1025r²)

⇒ New surface area = 4πr² × 1.1025

Percentage increase in surface area = (New surface area - Original surface area) / Original surface area × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (4πr² × 1.1025 - 4πr²) / 4πr² × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = (1.1025 - 1) × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 0.1025 × 100

⇒ Percentage increase = 10.25%

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: The base radius of a circular cylinder is 10.5 cm. If the area of its curved surface is 792 cm², then what is the volume of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The Volume and Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder are directly related.

Since Volume = πr²h and CSA = 2πrh, we can substitute CSA into the volume formula.

Volume = (CSA ÷ 2) × r

Volume = (792 ÷ 2) × 10.5

Volume = 396 × 10.5 = 4158 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 4158 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of base (r) = 10.5 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 792 cm²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10e023b2992b6c02a368c70008a4890599b279122cc49ccb0e12b3023d34037b.png] 

**Formula Used:**

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22 ÷ 7) × 10.5 × h = 792

⇒ 2 × 22 × 1.5 × h = 792

⇒ 66 × h = 792

⇒ h = 792 ÷ 66 = 12 cm

Now, substitute the value of height (h) to calculate the volume:

⇒ Volume = πr²h

⇒ Volume = (22 ÷ 7) × 10.5 × 10.5 × 12

⇒ Volume = 22 × 1.5 × 10.5 × 12

⇒ Volume = 33 × 126

⇒ Volume = 4158 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 4158 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular flat bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone vs Cylinder

A cone with the same base radius and height has exactly one-third the volume of the corresponding cylinder: V = (1 ÷ 3)πr²h.

Hollow Cylinder

For a hollow cylinder with outer radius R and inner radius r, the volume of the material used is given by V = π(R² − r²)h.
</p

questions.question: The radius and height of a cylinder are in the ratio 6 : 7 and its volume is 792 cm³. Calculate its curved surface area in cm².
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the radius to the height of the cylinder = 6 : 7

Volume of the cylinder = 792 cm³

**Formula used:**

Volume of a cylinder = πr²h

Curved surface area of a cylinder = 2πrh

**Calculation:**

Let the common ratio be x.

Then, the radius r = 6x and the height h = 7x.

Using the volume formula:

π(6x)²(7x) = 792

⇒ π × 36x² × 7x = 792

⇒ 252πx³ = 792

Take π as 22/7:

⇒ 252 × 22/7 × x³ = 792

⇒ 792x³ = 792

⇒ x³ = 1

⇒ x = 1

Thus, radius r = 6x = 6 × 1 = 6 cm

And height h = 7x = 7 × 1 = 7 cm

Now, calculate the curved surface area:

Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 6 × 7

= 2 × 22 × 6

= 264 cm²

**∴ The curved surface area of the cylinder is 264 cm².**

questions.question:
The curved surface area of a cone is 2200 cm² and its radius is 25 cm, what is the slant height (in cm) of the cone?

(Use pi=(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Curved surface area of a cone (CSA) = 2200 cm²

Radius (r) = 25 cm

Use π = 22/7

**Concept:**

The formula for the curved surface area of a cone is:

CSA = π × r × l

where l is the slant height.

**Calculation:**

We have:

⇒ 2200 = (22/7) × 25 × l

⇒ l = 2200 × (7/22) × (1/25)

⇒ l = 4 × 7

⇒ l = 28

**∴ The slant height (l) of the cone is 28 cm.**

questions.question: Find the length of the longest stick that can be fitted in a cubical vessel of edge 70 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The longest stick that can fit inside a 3D box corresponds to its main body diagonal.

For a cube with side length 'a', the body diagonal is given directly by the formula a√3.

Given the side of the cubical vessel a = 70 cm.

Longest stick = 70 × √3 = 70√3 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 70√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78dcfa92c2521df237f3e91a3ef7d1e592fee2ddd92041352e50b45a98dda561.png] 

**Given:**

Edge length of the cubical vessel (a) = 70 cm

**Formula Used:**

The length of the longest stick that can be fitted inside a regular cubical vessel is equal to the length of its main body diagonal.

Body Diagonal of a cube = √(a² + a² + a²) = a√3

**Calculations:**

⇒ Length of longest stick = 70 × √3

⇒ Length of longest stick = 70√3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 70√3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Cuboid

For a rectangular cuboid with length l, breadth b, and height h, the longest stick is its body diagonal given by √(l² + b² + h²).

Surface Area & Volume of a Cube

Volume = a³ | Total Surface Area = 6a² | Lateral (4-wall) Surface Area = 4a².

Inradius & Circumradius of a Cube

The radius of the largest sphere fitting inside (inradius) is a/2. The radius of the circumscribing sphere containing the cube (circumradius) is (a√3)/2.
</p

questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 11 cm is melted and recast into small solid spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many maximum number (in integer) of such spheres can be made?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of solid sphere = 11 cm

Radius of small solid sphere = 2 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

Number of small sphere = (Volume of solid sphere)/(Volume of small solid sphere)

Where, r = Radius of the sphere 

**Calculation:**

Volume of the solid sphere with radius 11 cm = (4/3) × π × 11³

Volume of the small solid sphere with radius 2 cm = (4/3) × π × 2³

Number of small solid sphere = (4/3) × π × 11³/(4/3) × π × 2³ = 1331/8 = 166.37 ≈ 166

**∴ Maximum 166 of such spheres can be made.**

questions.question: The height of a cylinder is 20 cm. The lateral surface area is 1760 cm². Its volume is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume formula includes π (22/7), meaning the final volume must perfectly be divisible by 11.

Check the given options for the divisibility rule of 11 (difference between the sum of alternating digits must be 0 or a multiple of 11).

Among the given options, only 12320 satisfies this condition: (1 + 3 + 0) − (2 + 2) = 4 − 4 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47055f9c2527d7c1b4f033c7dbf13e00bab0adee363a411599e2f749bf4077ce.png] 

**Given:**

Height of cylinder (h) = 20 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 1760 cm²

**Formula Used:**

LSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 20 = 1760

⇒ 880/7 × r = 1760

⇒ r = (1760 × 7) ÷ 880

⇒ r = 14 cm

Now, finding the volume using the radius:

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 14 × 14 × 20

⇒ Volume = 22 × 2 × 14 × 20

⇒ Volume = 44 × 280

⇒ Volume = 12320 cm³

⇒ Alternatively, Volume = (LSA ÷ 2) × r = (1760 ÷ 2) × 14 = 880 × 14 = 12320 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 12320 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the lateral area plus the two circular bases. Formula: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of the cylinder's volume. Formula: Volume = (1/3)πr²h.

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

For a hollow cylindrical pipe with outer radius R and inner radius r, the material volume is given by V = π(R² − r²)h.
</p
